gloss: to come in contact with; to adjoin; to receive, to treat

definitions.gloss: to come in contact with, to touch, to adjoin
definitions.explanation: To be physically adjacent to or in contact with something. Also used for encountering information, culture, or experiences.

definitions.gloss: to receive, to treat, to deal with
definitions.explanation: To interact with or treat a person in a particular manner.

examples.japanese: {海|うみ}に{接|せっ}する{町|まち}に{住|す}んでいる。
examples.english: I live in a town that borders the sea.

examples.japanese: {外国|がいこく}の{文化|ぶんか}に{接|せっ}する{機会|きかい}が{増|ふ}えた。
examples.english: Opportunities to encounter foreign culture have increased.

examples.japanese: {自然|しぜん}に{接|せっ}することで{心|こころ}が{癒|いや}される。
examples.english: Being in contact with nature heals the mind.

examples.japanese: {客|きゃく}に{丁寧|ていねい}に{接|せっ}する。
{子|こ}どもには{優|やさ}しく{接|せっ}してください。
examples.english: Please be gentle with the children.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はだれに{対|たい}しても{公平|こうへい}に{接|せっ}する{人|ひと}だ。
examples.english: He is someone who treats everyone fairly.

notes:
USAGE:
A special-class suru verb (not noun + する). Conjugates as {接|せっ}する, {接|せっ}して, {接|せっ}した. Sense 1 covers both physical adjacency and figurative contact (encountering culture, nature, art). Sense 2 focuses on interpersonal treatment and is very common in business and customer service contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ～に{接|せっ}する: to border, to be adjacent to; to come into contact with
- {人|ひと}に{接|せっ}する: to deal with people
- {態度|たいど}で{接|せっ}する: to treat with a certain attitude

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {触|ふ}れる: to touch (physical contact; also figurative)
- {隣接|りんせつ}する: to be adjacent (more formal, physical only)
